approach: The paper's exact system is the authors' own fastText C++ supervised trainer, and the repo ships classification-results.sh which downloads the Zhang et al. 8-dataset release and trains/evaluates every Table 1 row, so the plan is plumbing rather than re-implementation: get a working fasttext engine, get AG News in `__label__N` format, then run the authors' configuration `-dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr <lr> -thread 20`. A thin reproduce.py drives everything with the Python binding (fasttext-wheel on Windows, native build or `make` when a POSIX toolchain exists), reconstructs the missing validation split (10% of the 120k train set, assumption A4) to pick lr from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}, then retrains on the full training set and evaluates on the official 7.6k test set. The same driver also emits the no-bigram C2 row for free. Only results/metrics.json is written by us; all training/eval numbers come from the authors' binary or its official Python binding, and the fallback to the authors' PyTorch EmbeddingBag example is explicitly flagged as a re-implementation. Everything is CPU-only with 20 threads, matching the paper.
steps: Environment probe: print python version, os.cpu_count(), total RAM, and shutil.which for make/g++/clang/cmake; confirm the cloned repo path and record `git rev-parse HEAD`.

Read the authors' classification-results.sh and classification-example.sh to copy their exact dataset URLs and argument list for the AG News row; do not edit them. If a POSIX bash + make are available, running classification-results.sh directly is the preferred path and reproduce.py only parses/wraps its output.

Build/find the engine via fasttext_engine.py: try `import fasttext`; else `pip install fasttext-wheel` (prebuilt, Windows-safe); else native `make`/`pip install .`; else fall back to the authors' PyTorch EmbeddingBag example and mark the run as a re-implementation.

Download AG News with prepare_data.py (authors' URL first, then Zhang et al. CSV / HF mirror) and convert to `__label__1..4 <tokens>` lines; write data/ag_news.full.train (120k), data/ag_news.test (7.6k) and, with a fixed seed, data/ag_news.train (108k) + data/ag_news.valid (12k).

Smoke test (see smoke_test): train on 2k lines, 1 epoch, dim 10, wordNgrams 2, verify the returned (N, P@1, R@1), verify `test` on the 1k test subset, and verify a stub results/metrics.json round-trips.

lr search: for lr in {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} run the authors' trainer on data/ag_news.train with -dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr <lr> -thread 20 -minCount 1, evaluate on data/ag_news.valid, keep all four validation accuracies.

Final C1 run: pick the argmax-lr and retrain on the full 120k data/ag_news.full.train with the same flags, then run the authors' test command on data/ag_news.test (7.6k) and record P@1 as a percentage.
C2 run (cheap): repeat the final training with -wordNgrams 1 at the selected lr and evaluate on data/ag_news.test.

Write results/metrics.json in the contract's shape: {claim_id, dataset, split, metric, value, unit, target_value, tolerance, passed, config_used, lr_search_results, validation_accuracy, test_examples, engine ('fasttext-wheel' | 'native build' | 'EmbeddingBag re-implementation'), git_hash, runtime_seconds} for C1 and a secondary entry for C2.
Report: the C1 accuracy with |acc - 92.5| <= 1.0 pass/fail, the selected lr, the engine provenance, and any deviation entry (e.g., bucket=10M instead of A3's 100M).
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke  ->  builds a 2k-line train / 1k-line test subset from the converted AG News files, trains with dim=10, wordNgrams=2, epoch=1, lr=0.1, thread=4 via fasttext_engine.train(), then fasttext_engine.test() on the 1k subset; asserts that both calls return without error, that N matches the subset size, that P@1 is a float in [0,1], and that a stub results/metrics.json is written and reloadable. Runs in well under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Data sizes: data/ag_news.full.train == 120000 lines, data/ag_news.test == 7600 lines, search/valid split from the same 120000 lines (108000/12000) with no overlap (verify by hashing the first token+label of each line).
Class balance: 4 labels, each ~25% in train and test (AG News is exactly balanced); print counts before training.
Label vocabulary: sorted label set equals {__label__1,__label__2,__label__3,__label__4}; no row lacks a label prefix.
Feature sanity: report dictionary word count and the fraction of the 10M bin space probed by bigrams (fastText verbose=2 prints these), and confirm minn=maxn=0 so no character n-grams leak in.

Sanity baseline: unigram fastText (wordNgrams=1, 1 epoch, lr=0.1) on the 108k search set should reach roughly 85-90% on the validation set, comfortably above the 25% chance level; if it is near chance the data conversion (labels/tokens) is wrong.

Engine provenance check: print fasttext module version/`./fasttext --help` banner and assert the model file exists after training; if the EmbeddingBag fallback is used, set verdict_ceiling='partially_reproduced' in metrics.json.
Memory check before the final run: est. input matrix = (|V| + bucket) * dim * 4 bytes; if the 100M-bin variant (A3) would exceed available RAM, stay at bucket=10M and log the deviation.
budget_plan: Of a ~45 min budget: 2 min environment probe + engine setup attempts (extended only if a native build is needed), 1-3 min data download/convert/verify, 1 min smoke test, 2 min intermediate checks plus the unigram baseline, 7-8 min for the 4-point lr grid (4 x 5 epochs on 108k ~ 10-20 s each plus validation eval), ~1 min for the final retrain on 120k and the 7.6k test pass, ~1 min for the no-bigram C2 run, 2-3 min to write results/metrics.json and the report. Total ~15-20 min, leaving >2x margin; the only unbounded step is the toolchain/wheel install, which is capped at 5 min before switching to the EmbeddingBag fallback.

"""Optional extra datasets from Table 1 (run only if cheap and available).

The paper's Table 1 covers eight datasets and states that "FastText has been
run with the same parameters for all the datasets" (R7).  The target claim C1
only needs AG News, so the extras are strictly optional: they are skipped
silently when their raw csv release is not in REPRO_DATA_CACHE and cannot be
downloaded, and they are skipped when the overall run is already close to the
time budget.  A failure here can never affect the AG News numbers.

DBpedia is included because it is cheap (560k/70k short documents, ~27M
words).  Sogou is deliberately *not* included: its release is 1.2 GB of
pinyin-transliterated text (~320M words), which alone would cost ~15 minutes
of the 20-minute clean-re-run budget.
"""

import io
import json
import os
import random
import time

import config
import prepare_data

DATASETS = {
    "dbpedia": {
        "csv_subdir": "dbpedia_csv",
        "tar_name": "dbpedia_csv.tar.gz",
        "google_drive_id": "0Bz8a_Dbh9QhbQ2Vic1kxMmZZQ1k",
        "claim_id": "C4",
        "paper_target": 98.6,
        "n_train": 560000,
        "n_test": 70000,
        "n_classes": 14,
    },
}


def _paths(name):
    d = os.path.join(config.DATA_DIR, name)
    return {
        "full_train": os.path.join(d, name + ".full.train"),
        "search_train": os.path.join(d, name + ".train"),
        "valid": os.path.join(d, name + ".valid"),
        "test": os.path.join(d, name + ".test"),
    }


def _ensure_csvs(spec):
    d = os.path.join(config.CACHE, spec["csv_subdir"])
    if (os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "train.csv"))
            and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "test.csv"))):
        return d
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    tar = os.path.join(config.CACHE, spec["tar_name"])
    url = "https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=" + spec["google_drive_id"]
    try:
        prepare_data._download(url, tar)
        prepare_data._extract_tar(tar, config.CACHE)
    except Exception as exc:
        print("  download failed: %r" % (exc,))
    if (os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "train.csv"))
            and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "test.csv"))):
        return d
    raise RuntimeError("raw csv release for %s not available" % spec["csv_subdir"])


def build(name):
    spec = DATASETS[name]
    p = _paths(name)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p["full_train"]), exist_ok=True)
    if all(os.path.isfile(v) for v in p.values()):
        return p
    csv_dir = _ensure_csvs(spec)
    rng = random.Random(config.DATA_SEED)
    n_tr = prepare_data.convert(os.path.join(csv_dir, "train.csv"), p["full_train"], rng)
    n_te = prepare_data.convert(os.path.join(csv_dir, "test.csv"), p["test"], None)
    n_s, n_v = prepare_data.split_train_valid(p["full_train"], p["search_train"],
                                              p["valid"], config.VALID_FRACTION,
                                              config.DATA_SEED)
    print("  %s: full train %d, test %d, search train %d, valid %d"
          % (name, n_tr, n_te, n_s, n_v))
    return p


def run(ft, name, seeds):
    """Same protocol as AG News: lr search on a validation holdout, then a
    final run on the full training set evaluated on the official test split."""
    import fasttext_engine

    spec = DATASETS[name]
    print("=== EXTRA DATASET: %s (claim %s, paper target %.1f%%) ==="
          % (name, spec["claim_id"], spec["paper_target"]))
    p = build(name)

    def kw(wordNgrams, lr, seed):
        return dict(dim=config.DIM, wordNgrams=wordNgrams, epoch=config.EPOCH, lr=lr,
                    thread=config.THREAD, bucket=config.BUCKET, minCount=config.MINCOUNT,
                    minn=config.MINN, maxn=config.MAXN, loss=config.LOSS,
                    lrUpdateRate=config.LR_UPDATE_RATE, verbose=0, seed=seed)

    grid = []
    for lr in config.LR_GRID:
        model = fasttext_engine.train(ft, p["search_train"], **kw(config.WORDNGRAMS, lr, seeds[0]))
        n, acc, _ = fasttext_engine.test(model, p["valid"])
        acc *= 100.0
        grid.append({"lr": lr, "valid_accuracy": round(acc, 4)})
        print("  lr=%-5s valid P@1 = %.3f%%" % (lr, acc))
    best = max(grid, key=lambda r: r["valid_accuracy"])
    print("  selected lr = %s" % best["lr"])

    out = {"dataset": name, "claim_id": spec["claim_id"],
           "paper_target": spec["paper_target"], "lr_grid": grid,
           "selected_lr": best["lr"], "seeds": seeds, "rows": {}}
    for tag, wordNgrams in (("bigram", config.WORDNGRAMS), ("no_bigram", 1)):
        accs = []
        for seed in seeds:
            model = fasttext_engine.train(ft, p["full_train"], **kw(wordNgrams, best["lr"], seed))
            n, acc, _ = fasttext_engine.test(model, p["test"])
            accs.append(round(100.0 * acc, 4))
        mean = sum(accs) / len(accs)
        out["rows"][tag] = {"wordNgrams": wordNgrams, "lr": best["lr"],
                            "per_seed_test_accuracy": accs,
                            "mean_test_accuracy": round(mean, 4),
                            "test_examples": n}
        print("  %s: mean test P@1 = %.3f%% (per seed %s)"
              % (tag, mean, accs))
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import fasttext_engine
    ft, prov = fasttext_engine.get_engine()
    print(json.dumps(run(ft, "dbpedia", [1]), indent=2))

target.statement: fastText with 10 hidden units and bigram features achieves 92.5% test accuracy on AG News.
target.table_ref: Table 1, row fastText, h = 10, bigram, column AG

tolerance.why: AG News test accuracy is a percentage on a large fixed test set, and the paper reports no confidence interval. A 1.0 absolute band covers normal run-to-run variation, one-decimal rounding, and the undisclosed learning-rate choice from the paper's small validation grid.

audit_summary: Claim C1 (AG News, fastText h=10 with bigrams, 92.5%) is matched at 92.350% +/- 0.10 over 5 seeds (|diff| 0.15 pp against a 1.0 pp tolerance), and the clean re-run reproduces it end to end in 462 s from a wiped results/ and data/ directory with the same per-seed numbers (92.211-92.513), so nothing is hard-coded: 92.5 appears in the code only as TARGET_VALUE for the pass/fail comparison and in print statements. The experiment is the right one - the authors' own fastText 0.9.2 C++ supervised trainer (prebuilt wheel of the same facebookresearch sources), the Zhang et al. 120k/7.6k AG News split, the authors' normalize_text tokenizer, dim=10, wordNgrams=2, epoch=5, thread=20, and an lr drawn from the paper's grid and selected on a 12k validation holdout carved from train while the 7,600-line official test set stayed untouched during tuning. Two real fidelity gaps are documented rather than hidden: loss='softmax' instead of the hierarchical softmax of Sec 2.1 (R4/R12 missing, flagged as method substituted - though the authors' own classification-results.sh also passes no -loss flag, so 92.5 was itself produced with softmax and the accuracy effect for k=4 is negligible), and bucket=10M instead of the 100M bins Sec 2.2 prescribes for unigram+bigram (A15). Only the AG News row was attempted; the other Table 1 datasets and the YFCC100M tag-prediction claim were skipped, so R7 and R10 are unmet for the extra claims. Nothing was scaled down relative to the target: full 120k training set, full test split, the complete lr grid, and more seeds than the paper's single run.

requirement_check.evidence: fastText supervised builds a bag of unigrams plus hashed bigrams (config: wordNgrams=2, bucket=10,000,000, minn=maxn=0 so no char n-grams); the verbose training log shows a 91,095-word dictionary and the model normalizes by averaging the feature embeddings. Bigrams are the exact difference between the C1 and C2 runs (92.350 vs 91.292), confirming they are actually used.

fastText's supervised model is lookup table A (dim=10 = h) -> mean of the document's feature embeddings -> linear layer B -> 4-way softmax; this is the authors' own C++ trainer (fasttext-wheel 0.9.2, same facebookresearch/fastText sources), not a re-implementation.

loss='softmax' in fastText minimizes the negative log-likelihood over the 4 classes; avg.loss is printed in the training log (0.695 after 5 epochs), and per-seed test accuracy is computed by model.test on held-out data.

config.LOSS='softmax'; no -loss hs and no Huffman coding tree anywhere in the run. Logged as assumption A17 with the (correct) justification that the authors' classification-results.sh passes no -loss flag, so the published 92.5 was itself produced with full softmax; nevertheless the paper's stated Section 2.1 method is not implemented.

thread=20 passed to fastText (asynchronous hogwild-style SGD over 20 threads); lrUpdateRate=100 yields fastText's linear decay, and the log shows lr falling 0.25 -> 0.0 linearly across the 5 epochs (avg.loss 1.22 -> 0.70).

dim=10, epoch=5; the grid {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5} was searched on a 12,000-line validation holdout with 3 seeds per point (lr_search_log.json / metrics.json lr_search), selecting lr=0.25 (mean valid 92.572%).

Only AG News was run; Sogou, DBpedia, Yelp P./F., Yahoo and Amazon were deliberately skipped. The same config dict is applied identically to the C1 and C2 runs, but cross-dataset consistency (the actual content of R7) is untested.

The hashing trick is used through fastText's own bucket hashing, but bucket=10,000,000 rather than the 100M bins Sec 2.2 prescribes for a unigram+bigram feature set (A15). The deviation is disclosed in metrics.json notes; 10M matches the authors' classification-results.sh and is far more than the ~90k words need.

Data are the Zhang et al. (2015) AG News release: 120,000 train / 7,600 test lines verified by intermediate checks, labels exactly {__label__1..4}, converted line-for-line with a Python port of the authors' normalize_text() from repo/classification-results.sh, tested on the untouched official test split.
YFCC100M tag prediction (h=200, bigrams, 5 epochs, precision@1) was not attempted; extra_claims is empty and the implementer states this row was deliberately out of scope for the C1 match target.
All training/testing is CPU-only with thread=20 as specified; the host has fewer physical cores than 20 logical threads, which is disclosed in metrics.json notes.
Test-time prediction is a full 4-way softmax argmax (model.test), not a Huffman-tree traversal with the binary-heap T-top extension; a direct consequence of the softmax choice for R4.
